row.title: Felsner–Krawczyk–Micek conjecture for poset antichains
row.statement:
For a positive integer $k$, let $\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{k}$ be the poset consisting of two disjoint $k$-element chains with no comparabilities between distinct chains. Let $\mathcal{P}(k)$ be the class of posets containing no subposet isomorphic to $\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{k}$, and let $\mathcal{P}(k,w)$ be the subclass consisting of posets of width at most $w$. For a poset $P$, write $\mathcal{M}(P)$ for its family of maximum antichains. **Felsner–Krawczyk–Micek conjecture.** For positive integers $k,w$ with $k\ge 2$, the maximum width of $\mathcal{M}(P)$ over posets $P\in\mathcal{P}(k,w)$ is

$$
(k-1)^{w-1}.
$$

This conjecture is an equivalent poset formulation of the crossing-vector extremal problem, using the bound relating the width of the family of maximum antichains to $f(k-1,w)$. Its general status is not resolved in the supplied text.
row.source_name: Michał Lasoń, Piotr Micek, Noah Streib, William T. Trotter and Bartosz Walczak, “An extremal problem on crossing vectors”, arXiv:1205.1824 (2014).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.1824

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2012).

row.title: Color count conjecture for highly colorable maps
row.statement:
Let $n\geq 2$. Define $m_1(n),m_2(n),m_3(n),m_4(n)$ to be the four largest possible numbers of valid color vectors, modulo the action of $S_3$ on the colors, among tree pairs corresponding to maps in $\mathfrak W$ and having $n$ internal vertices each, with

$$
m_4(n)<m_3(n)<m_2(n)<m_1(n).
$$

Let $J(n)$ denote the Jacobsthal numbers, and write $f(n)+(e,o)$ for $f(n)+e$ when $n$ is even and $f(n)+o$ when $n$ is odd. **Color count conjecture.** The following hold:

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_1(n)&=J(n-3)+(1,0),&& n\geq 5,\\
m_2(n)&=J(n-4)+(7,5)=m_1(n-1)+(7,4),&& n\geq 7,\\
m_3(n)&=J(n-4)+(1,0)=m_1(n-1),&& n\geq 7,\\
m_4(n)&=J(n-4)-(1,2)=m_1(n-1)-(1,3),&& n\geq 7.
\end{aligned}
$$

These formulas are based on computational observations about the numbers of colorings of maps in $\mathfrak W$. The authors state that they are unable to determine the quantities in general and present these formulas as conjectural estimates; the supplied text gives no resolution.
row.source_name: Garry Bowlin and Matthew G. Brin, “Coloring Planar Graphs via Colored Paths in the Associahedra”, arXiv:1301.3984 (2013).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1301.3984

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2013).

row.title: Bauer–Fan–Veldman circumference conjecture for 1-tough graphs
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, let $\tau(G)$ denote its toughness, let $\rho(G)$ denote the independence number, and let $\sigma_3(G)$ be its smallest union degree of order $3$:

$$
\sigma_3(G)=\begin{cases}\min\{\deg(v_1)+\deg(v_2)+\deg(v_3):\{v_1,v_2,v_3\}\text{ is independent}\},&\rho(G)\geq 3,\\3(n-1),&\rho(G)<3.\end{cases}
$$

For nonadjacent vertices $u,v$ at distance $2$, write $N(u,v)=N(u)\cup N(v)$, and define

$$
NC2(G)=\begin{cases}\min\{|N(u)\cup N(v)|:d(u,v)=2\},&G\text{ is not complete},\
-1,&G\text{ is complete}.\end{cases}
$$

Let $c(G)$ be the circumference of $G$, namely the length of a longest cycle. **Bauer–Fan–Veldman conjecture.** If $G$ is a 1-tough graph with $\sigma_3(G)\geq n\geq 3$, then

$$
c(G)\geq\min\{n,2NC2(G)+4\}.
$$

This strengthens the earlier lower bound $c(G)\geq\min\{n,2NC2(G)\}$; the intermediate bound with additive constant $2$ follows from a theorem of Hoa. The conjecture is the claim proved in the source paper.
row.source_name: Tri Lai, “Proof of a conjecture of Bauer, Fan and Veldman”, arXiv:1309.5379 (2013).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.5379

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of September 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

row.title: Ilić and Ilić's minimum Laplacian-coefficient conjecture for unicyclic graphs
row.statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}_{n,l}$ be the set of $n$-vertex unicyclic graphs with $l$ leaves, and let $U_{n,l}^{3,0}$ be the balanced starlike unicyclic graph of order $n$, with $l$ leaves and girth $3$, obtained with attachment parameter $p=0$. For graphs on $n$ vertices, write $G\preceq H$ when every Laplacian coefficient of $G$ is at most the corresponding coefficient of $H$.

**Ilić and Ilić's conjecture.** Among all $n$-vertex unicyclic graphs, the graph $U_{n,l}^{3,0}$ has the minimum Laplacian coefficients $c_k$, $k=0,\dots,n$; equivalently, $U_{n,l}^{3,0}$ is the only minimal element in the poset $(\mathcal{U}_{n,l},\preceq)$.

The conjecture concerns the simultaneous minimization of all Laplacian coefficients within unicyclic graphs with a fixed number of leaves. It is explicitly stated later in the paper to be false, so the original conjecture is refuted.
row.source_name: Jie Zhang and Xiao-Dong Zhang, “Laplacian coefficients of unicyclic graphs with the number of leaves and girth”, arXiv:1311.1987 (2013).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.1987

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

row.title: Necessity of the singleton-partition condition for omnivocal communication
row.statement:
Let $X_{[m]}=(X_1,\ldots,X_m)$ be a multiterminal source model with $m\geq 3$ terminals. Let **omnivocal communication** mean communication in which every terminal communicates, and let the **singleton partition** be the partition $\{\{1\},\ldots,\{m\}\}$; write $\mathbf{I}(X_{[m]})$ for the source-model partition functional and call a partition a minimizer when it attains the minimum of this functional.

**Omnivocality conjecture.** Omnivocal communication is necessary for achieving SK capacity if and only if the singleton partition is the unique minimizer for $\mathbf{I}(X_{[m]})$.

This conjecture proposes that the sufficient condition established in the paper exactly characterizes when every terminal must communicate to achieve secret-key capacity. The condition is known to be sufficient in the stated setting, while the paper reports that necessity is proved only for $m=3$; the general case remains open.
row.source_name: Manuj Mukherjee, Navin Kashyap and Yogesh Sankarasubramaniam, “Achieving SK Capacity in the Source Model: When Must All Terminals Talk?”, arXiv:1401.5037 (2014).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.5037

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).

row.title: The three-colour decomposition conjecture for locally irregular graphs
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. A graph is **locally irregular** if every pair of adjacent vertices has distinct degrees. A decomposition into $3$ locally irregular subgraphs is a partition of $E(G)$ into three sets, each inducing a locally irregular subgraph of $G$. Let $\mathfrak{T}$ be the family of maximum-degree-$3$ graphs constructed from a triangle by repeatedly choosing a triangle with a vertex of degree $2$ and appending either a hanging path of even length or a hanging path of odd length with a triangle attached at its other end.

**Three-colour decomposition conjecture.** Every connected graph $G$ which does not belong to $\mathfrak{T}$ and is neither an odd-length path nor an odd-length cycle can be decomposed into $3$ locally irregular subgraphs.

The excluded graphs were subsequently shown to be exactly the connected graphs that admit no decomposition into any number of locally irregular subgraphs, so this conjecture is solved.
row.source_name: Jakub Przybyło, “On decomposing graphs of large minimum degree into locally irregular subgraphs”, arXiv:1508.01129 (2015).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.01129

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2015). “The graphs excluded in the conjecture above were also proven to be the only connected graphs which do not admit decompositions into any number of locally irregular subgraphs.”

row.title: Simplex and cube extremality conjecture for the Monge–Ampère eigenvalue
row.statement:
Let $n\geq 2$. A bounded open convex set in $\mathbb R^n$ has fixed positive volume, and the **Monge–Ampère eigenvalue** is the principal eigenvalue associated with the Monge–Ampère operator on that set. In the centrally symmetric case, assume the set is open, bounded, convex, and centrally symmetric.

**Simplex and cube extremality conjecture.** (i) Among all bounded open convex sets in $\mathbb R^n$ having a fixed positive volume, the $n$-dimensional regular simplex—the interior of the convex hull of $n+1$ equally spaced points in $\mathbb R^n$—has the smallest Monge–Ampère eigenvalue. (ii) Among all open bounded centrally symmetric convex sets in $\mathbb R^n$ having a fixed positive volume, the $n$-dimensional cube has the smallest Monge–Ampère eigenvalue.

The conjecture identifies the proposed minimizers in the extremal inequalities for the Monge–Ampère eigenvalue, motivated by Ball's reverse isoperimetric inequality. The cited context indicates that determining the extremal convex sets remains an open problem, including both the general and centrally symmetric cases.
row.source_name: Nam Q. Le, “The eigenvalue problem for the Monge-Ampère operator on general bounded convex domains”, arXiv:1701.05165 (2017).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05165

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2017).

row.title: A weighted Complete Intersection conjecture for Lagrangians
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a $t$-intersecting $r$-graph, meaning that any two edges of $G$ have intersection of size at least $t$. For integers $t\geq 1$, $i\geq 0$, and $r\geq t+i$, let $F(r,t,i)$ be the $(\leq r)$-graph on $[t+2i]$ whose edges have sizes between $t+i$ and $r$. For a weighting $p:[t+2i]^+\to[0,1]$, write $w_p(F(r,t,i))$ for the corresponding weighted edge sum, and require $(F(r,t,i),t+2i,p)$ to be a weighted $t$-intersecting set system. **Weighted Complete Intersection conjecture.** Then

$$
r!\lambda(G)\leq\max_{0\leq i\leq r-t}w_p(F(r,t,i)),
$$

where the maximum is implicitly taken over all such weightings $p$. This would extend the Complete Intersection Theorem from edge counts to Lagrangians of $t$-intersecting $r$-graphs; the supplied text presents it as a question toward a complete intersection theorem, and gives no resolution.
row.source_name: Adam Bene Watts, Sergey Norin and Liana Yepremyan, “A Turán theorem for extensions via an Erdős-Ko-Rado theorem for Lagrangians”, arXiv:1707.01533 (2017).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.01533

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

row.title: Exact rainbow-extremal sets for restricted sum-free colorings
row.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For a subset $A\subseteq[n]$, let $g(A,r)$ denote the number of rainbow sum-free $r$-colorings of $A$, and let $g(n,r)=\max_{A\subseteq[n]}g(A,r)$. A set attaining this maximum is called a **rainbow $r$-extremal set**. For even $n$, define

$$
I_1=\left[\frac{n}{2}-1,n\right],\qquad I_2=\left[\frac{n}{2},n\right],
$$

and for odd $n$ define

$$
I_3=\left[\frac{n-1}{2},n\right].
$$

**Exact-extremal-set conjecture.** Let $n,r$ be positive integers with $r\geq4$. If $n$ is even and $r\leq7$, then

$$
g(n,r)=r^{n/2}\left(3-\frac{2}{r}\right)^2,
$$

and $I_1$ is the unique rainbow $r$-extremal set. If $n$ is even and $r\geq8$, then $g(n,r)=r^{n/2+1}$, and $I_2$ is the unique rainbow $r$-extremal set. If $n$ is odd and $r=4$, then $g(n,r)=g([n],r)$, and $[n]$ is the unique rainbow $r$-extremal set. If $n$ is odd and $r\geq5$, then

$$
g(n,r)=r^{\lceil n/2\rceil}\left(3-\frac{2}{r}\right),
$$

and $I_3$ is the unique rainbow $r$-extremal set.

The paper proves the corresponding extremal results for $r\leq3$ and $r\geq8$; the exact structure remains unresolved for $4\leq r\leq7$, making these cases the central open part of the conjecture.
row.source_name: Yangyang Cheng, Yifan Jing, Lina Li, Guanghui Wang and Wenling Zhou, “Integer colorings with forbidden rainbow sums”, arXiv:2005.14384 (2023).
row.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1710.08025](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.08025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14384

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

row.title: Conjecture on extremal real equiangular tight frames
row.statement:
Let $d\geq 5$. An **equiangular tight frame (ETF)** with parameters $(d,n)$ is a real ETF for $\mathbb{R}^d$ of size $n$. **ETF extension conjecture.** There exists an ETF with parameters

$$
\left(d+1,\frac{(d+1)(d+2)}{2}\right)
$$

if and only if there exists an ETF with parameters

$$
\left(d,\frac{d(d+2)}{3}\right).
$$

The conjecture relates two extremal ETF sizes arising from antipodal spherical designs and would connect the existence of the known configurations in dimensions $6$ and $22$ with corresponding larger ETFs. Its status is not resolved in the source.
row.source_name: Zhiqiang Xu, Zili Xu and Wei-Hsuan Yu, “Bounds on antipodal spherical designs with few angles”, arXiv:2007.13999 (2020).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.13999

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2020).

row.title: Irreducibility conjecture for cell representations of the two Gelfand $W$-graphs of $S_n$
row.statement: Let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $\Gamma^\mathbf{m}(S_n)$ and $\Gamma^\mathbf{n}(S_n)$ be the two Gelfand $W$-graphs considered in the paper. Their cell representations are the representations associated to the cells of these graphs. **Irreducibility conjecture.** The cell representations associated to $\Gamma^\mathbf{m}(S_n)$ and $\Gamma^\mathbf{n}(S_n)$ are all irreducible. This conjecture is stated as holding at least for $n\leq 10$; the source contrasts it with the behavior in types $\mathsf{BC}$ and $\mathsf{D}$, where it does not hold in the same form.
row.source_name: Eric Marberg and Yifeng Zhang, “Gelfand W-graphs for classical Weyl groups”, arXiv:2012.13868 (2021).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.13868

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

row.title: The sun and balanced double sun conjecture for maximal Randić energy
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, and let $RE(G)$ denote its Randić energy. A **sun** and a **balanced double sun** are the graphs described in Figure 2 of Gutman, Furtula and Bozkurt (2014).

**Sun and balanced double sun conjecture.** The connected graph of odd order $n\geq 1$ having maximal Randić energy is the sun. The connected graph of even order $n\geq 2$ having maximal Randić energy is the balanced double sun.

This is a more specific conjecture about the extremal connected graph and remains open. It is consistent with the broader conjecture that every connected graph with maximal Randić energy is a tree.
row.source_name: Domingos M. Cardoso, Paula Carvalho, Roberto C. Díaz and Paula Rama, “On the Randić energy of caterpillar graphs”, arXiv:2107.11422 (2021).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.11422

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2021). “The following more thinner conjecture, also posed in , remains open too.”

row.title: Affine fully commutative element enumeration conjecture for $G(m,m,n)$
row.statement:
Let $a_m$ denote the number of fully commutative elements in $G(m,m,n)$, for $n\geq 3$, with the affine generating set. **Affine enumeration conjecture.** There is a positive integer $k$ such that

$$
a_{m+1}=a_m+k.
$$

In particular, $k=12$ when $n=3$ and $k=60$ when $n=4$. The conjecture is suggested by the enumerative data for $G(m,m,3)$ and $G(m,m,4)$; the general assertion and the specified constants remain unproved in the supplied source.
row.source_name: Jiayuan Wang, “A note on fully commutative elements in complex reflection groups”, arXiv:2109.09773 (2021).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.09773

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

row.title: Herden's congruence conjecture for 2-regular partitions with designated summands
row.statement:
Let $PD_2(n)$ denote the number of $2$-regular partitions of $n$ with designated summands; equivalently, these are partitions into odd parts with exactly one occurrence of each distinct part designated. For $n\geq 0$, **Herden's congruence conjecture.**

$$
\begin{gathered}
PD_2(16n+12)\equiv 0 \pmod{4},\\
PD_2(24n+20)\equiv 0 \pmod{4},\\
PD_2(25n+5)\equiv 0 \pmod{4},\\
PD_2(32n+24)\equiv 0 \pmod{4},\\
PD_2(48n+26)\equiv 0 \pmod{4}.
\end{gathered}
$$

These are Ramanujan-like congruences for the counting function of partitions with designated summands restricted to odd parts. The source presents them as a conjecture inherited from earlier work; no resolution is supplied here.
row.source_name: James A. Sellers, “New Infinite Families of Congruences Modulo Powers of 2 for 2–Regular Partitions with Designated Summands”, arXiv:2306.15130 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.15130

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

row.title: Bowler–Brown–Fenner common-card bound for trees and connected non-trees
row.statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on $n$ vertices, where one is a tree and the other is a connected non-tree. A **common card** is an unlabeled graph occurring as a card in the decks of both $G$ and $H$. **Bowler–Brown–Fenner conjecture.** For $n\geq 44$, the only pair of graphs on $n$ vertices having at least $\lfloor \frac{2}{5}(n+1)\rfloor$ common cards is the pair found in Theorem 3.6 of Bowler, Brown, and Fenner. This conjecture concerns the extremal overlap between the decks of trees and connected non-trees; the source does not state whether it has been resolved.
row.source_name: Gabriëlle Zwaneveld, “Recognizing trees from incomplete decks”, arXiv:2311.16665 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.16665

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2023). “Although this conjecture is still open, we know that many graph properties can be deduced from the deck.”

row.title: The even-intersection bound for strongly restricted set systems
row.statement:
Let $t, k$ be integers with $t\geq 2$ and $2t-2>k$. If $(\mathcal A_1, \ldots, \mathcal A_k)$ are set families of an $n$ element set with

$$
\mathcal A_j=\{A_{j, i}: i\in [m]\}
$$

where $\left|\bigcap_{j=1}^k A_{j, i_j}\right|$ is even if and only if at least $t$ of the indices $i_j$ are distinct, then the family size should satisfy

$$
m=O\left(n^{1/\lfloor k/2\rfloor}\right).
$$

This conjecture concerns quantitative bounds for set systems whose intersection parity is determined exactly by the number of distinct selected indices. The paper states that it partially confirms a conjecture from 2022 as a byproduct of its main results; the supplied excerpt does not establish whether this precise bound is resolved, so its status is recorded as open.
row.source_name: Xin Wei, Xiande Zhang and Gennian Ge, “On set systems with strongly restricted intersections”, arXiv:2404.08280 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.08280

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

row.title: Conjectured exact value of the Ramsey number of a book graph versus an odd cycle
row.statement:
Let $B_n$ denote the book graph with $n$ pages and let $C_m$ denote the cycle of odd length $m$. The Ramsey number $R(B_n,C_m)$ is the least integer such that every red-blue edge-colouring of a complete graph of that order contains a red copy of $B_n$ or a blue copy of $C_m$.

**The authors' conjecture.** For each integer $n\geq 3493$, if $n\geq 2m+499$ and $m\geq 7$ is an odd integer, then

$$
R(B_n,C_m)=2n+3.
$$

The paper presents this as a conjecture motivated by the lower bound and notes that an earlier theorem partially confirms it for larger values of $n$. The authors also state that they proved the analogous claim for the subgraph $\mathbb{K}_{2,n}$ of $B_n$; the exact Ramsey-number assertion remains open in the supplied text.
row.source_name: Sayan Gupta, “A study of two Ramsey numbers involving odd cycles”, arXiv:2504.15693 (2025).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15693

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2025). “The conjecture was proved by Conlon .”

row.title: Lévêque et al.'s 4-color conjecture for ISK4-free graphs
row.statement: All graphs under consideration are finite and simple. A graph is **ISK4-free** if it contains no induced subdivision of $K_4$. **Lévêque et al.'s 4-color conjecture.** Every ISK4-free graph is $4$-colorable. Lévêque et al. showed that the chromatic number of ISK4-free graphs is bounded by a constant $c\geq 2^{512}$; subsequent work improved the known upper bound to $8$, while the conjectured bound of $4$ remains open.
row.source_name: Feng Liu, Shuang Sun and Yan Wang, “On the structures of diamond, bowtie-free graphs that do not contain an induced subdivision of K_4”, arXiv:2603.17645 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.17645

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of March 2026). “This conjecture was disproved by Pawlik et al. .”

row.title: The no-pinned-entry construction conjecture for even-order latin squares
row.statement: Let $n\geqslant 28$ be an even integer. A **latin square** of order $n$ is an $n\times n$ array in which each symbol occurs exactly once in each row and column, and a **transversal** is a selection of $n$ entries containing one representative of every row, column, and symbol. An entry is **pinned** if it belongs to every transversal. **No-pinned-entry construction conjecture.** There is a latin square of order $n$ that has no two disjoint transversals, but also has no pinned entry. The claim gives even-order latin squares whose transversals pairwise intersect without all sharing one entry; the paper states that its constructions support the conjecture, but that a general argument guaranteeing the required transversals is not known.
row.source_name: Afsane Ghafari and Ian M. Wanless, “Latin Squares whose transversals intersect in unusual ways”, arXiv:2607.17547 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17547

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

row.title: Nonexistence conjecture for 8-regular K3-irregular graphs
row.statement:
Let $G$ be an $8$-regular graph. For a vertex $v$ of $G$, let its $K_3$-degree be the number of subgraphs isomorphic to $K_3$ that contain $v$. The graph $G$ is **$K_3$-irregular** if its vertices do not all have distinct $K_3$-degrees.

**Nonexistence conjecture.** There are no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graphs.

The conjecture would improve the bounds obtained in the paper, which show that any $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph would have order between $17$ and $22$. The preceding heuristic search found examples with exactly two equal pairs of $K_3$-degrees for orders $19$, $20$, $21$, and $22$, so the conjecture remains open based on the supplied text.
row.source_name: Artem Hak, Sergiy Kozerenko and Andrii Serdiuk, “Regular K_3-irregular graphs”, arXiv:2507.18776 (2025).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18776

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).
